prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural‑language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), visible actions, interactions, and the setting; remain concrete, image‑centered and avoid speculation or subjective judgments. For every visible person state posture (for example, "standing upright," "sitting, weight shifted onto left leg," "leaning slightly forward"), orientation to the camera (facing, in profile, back to the camera), and whether they are stationary or moving; when describing motion give horizontal direction first then vertical relative to the image frame (for example, "from left to right," "toward the camera while descending"), name any visibly apparent phase of motion (starting/ascending/peaking/descending/landing) and indicate whether motions are simultaneous or sequential. For each moving subject describe trajectory both relative to the main subject (passing to her right, approaching from behind, moving alongside) and relative to the camera (toward/away from the camera, to the left/right edge of the frame), and for groups specify whether people are moving alone or as part of a group. Describe head orientation and precise gaze for every visible person (for example, "looking directly at the camera," "eyes down at a phone," "gaze up and to the left"). When people interact, report only observable interaction cues and roles using evident signs (open mouth facing another as an indicator of speaking; turned body, raised hand or pointing as gestures; facing and still with closed mouth as listening). For objects in contact or use, state exactly how the subject is using them (holding, gripping, resting, pulling, supporting, leaning on), which hand and side (left/right), whether the hand is in contact, gripping, merely near, or in motion versus resting, and describe the object's visible form (for example, "printed document," "rolled-up paper," "cylindrical thermos," "smartphone") rather than vague labels. Clarify precise spatial relationships, counts, arrangement, proximity and scale using camera‑relative language and clear phrases (foreground/midground/background; left/middle/right of frame; directly in front of/behind; a few feet/meters apart; clustered closely; in a line or scattered) and state the subject's placement relative to background elements (for example, "positioned centrally in front of a red backdrop," "standing to the left of a market stall"). Describe lighting, shadows and visible surface textures with observable cues and an approximate shadow direction or length when apparent, and report facial expressions or affect only when clearly evident using specific observable detail. Keep the caption concise, factual and single‑sentence. Output exactly one single sentence.
